text.p: Bangladesh has appointed a committee of advisers to assist Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria in formulating and implementing economic reforms, officials said on Thursday.
The move follows widespread criticism of the minister by opposition parties and some businessmen over his handling of major economic issues, in particular recent turbulence in the stock market.
The share index of the Dhaka Stock Exchange dropped to 1,280.27 on Wednesday from 1,782.36 one month ago and 1,962.31 at end of January.
One of the 14 committee members, Dr Wahid Uddin Mahmud, said the group would help the government on planning and handling of delicate economic issues, including policy matters.
But he added that the "formation of the committee is not enough... how the counselling is being implemented is important.

The committee, which will meet finance minister once every two months, will advise on "macro-economic indicators, revenue income and tax reforms, savings and investment situation, transparency, efficient management and supervision of the bank and financial institutions".
Bangladesh's overseas donors emphasised at a meeting in Dhaka last month that the government might require advice in these areas, finance ministry officials said.
The committee will also advise the government on foreign exchange adjustment policy and growth in all major sectors including agriculture and industry.
